title: Yara and the Thorn
premise: Yara, who has lived twelve years in the city of Vell as 'Lena Reyes,' a bone-carver selling harmless charms under a false name after magic was outlawed, discovers the old gods are answering prayers again because the covenant binding their realm to the mortal one is shattering. Hunted by the Inquisitor's wardens and betrayed by the found family she built on lies, she must journey to the Thorn, the broken axis where the covenant was first forged, and reforge it with a truth: her own name, spoken before gods and mortals alike. She succeeds at terrible cost, sacrificing her hearing of the dead to seal the realms, and returns to Vell as herself for the first time.
about_author: Edmund Hartwell is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing folk charms in coastal libraries before turning to fiction. He writes fantasy about quiet people carrying loud secrets, and lives near the sea with an opinionated cat.

chapters.title: The Charm That Answered
chapters.summary: Yara carves a mourning charm for a grieving fishwife and is horrified when it actually works—the dead speak back through the bone. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: dread beneath routine; the first crack in twelve years of careful silence as she realizes the outlawed magic isn't gone, it's waking.

chapters.title: Wardens at the Door
chapters.summary: Inquisitor Sarel Voss arrives in Vell investigating answered prayers, and Yara's adopted family—the tinker Bram and runaway scribe Odile—cover for her without knowing why. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: warmth and guilt entwined; she sees how much they'd risk for a woman whose name they don't truly know.

chapters.title: What the Dead Remember
chapters.summary: Following the voices in the bone, Yara finds a drowned shrine where a minor god, the Ferryman's daughter, begs her to carry word that the covenant is failing. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: reluctant awe; the dead give her a purpose she never asked for and a glimpse of her mother's voice among them.

chapters.title: The Tinker's Oath
chapters.summary: Bram reveals he once served the god-tenders and swore an oath he broke; Odile confesses she copied forbidden rites to survive. POV: alternating Yara and Bram. Emotional beat: found family deepening through shared shame—everyone in this household is hiding something holy or criminal.

chapters.title: Ashes of the God-Tenders
chapters.summary: The four flee Vell ahead of Voss's wardens, following an old pilgrim road littered with desecrated shrines. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: grief and resolve; Odile's scholarly knowledge becomes their map, and Yara begins trusting them with fragments of her real past.

chapters.title: The Inquisitor's Mercy
chapters.summary: Voss corners them at a river crossing but hesitates—she too has heard a prayer answered, her dead brother's voice. POV: Voss. Emotional beat: antagonist humanized; duty wars with wonder, and she lets them go, marking Yara's face so she can find her again.

chapters.title: Thornfall
chapters.summary: They reach the Thorn, the shattered axis-stone where heaven and earth were joined, and learn the covenant can only be reforged by someone who belongs wholly to neither realm—a liminal soul speaking their true name. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: devastating clarity; her false life was never escape, it was preparation.

chapters.title: The Name Beneath the Skin
chapters.summary: Yara finally tells Bram and Odile everything: her birth among the god-tenders, the purge, the name she buried. They refuse to let her face the rite alone. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: catharsis; truth costs her the safe fiction of Lena Reyes but wins her a family that knows her completely.

chapters.title: The Reforging
chapters.summary: At the Thorn, with Voss arriving torn between arrest and aid, Yara speaks her true name and offers her hearing of the dead as the covenant's new binding. The realms seal; the voices go silent forever. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: climax and sacrifice—she saves both worlds by giving up the gift that defined her.

chapters.title: A Quiet House in Vell
chapters.summary: Months later, magic is legal again and shrines reopen. Yara, deaf now to the dead, carves ordinary charms in a shop above Bram's forge while Odile records the restored rites. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: bittersweet peace; she has lost the voices but gained her name, her family, and at last a self worth signing her work with.
